subject: Runtime adoption playbook & schema adapter milestones
messages:
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@novacare.ai>
To: maya_srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@novacare.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Runtime adoption — next steps for streaming & output contract

Hi Maya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The team was really impressed with the low-latency streaming and the function-calling examples. Before we commit to Dedicated, we need a concrete implementation plan for: streaming delivery guarantees, how tool/function calls will be proxied from our runtime, and the JSON schema contract for structured outputs.

I've attached an internal schema draft (nova_schema_v1.json) to show our expectations for claim/diagnostic objects. Can Redwood provide:
- a short adoption playbook that maps milestones to deliverables (code + schema tests),
- a recommended adapter pattern for handling tool-call routing, and
- a minimal set of regression tests we can run during onboarding.

Timing is tight — procurement wants a high-level M.A.P. (mutual action plan) by next week.

Appreciate the help,
Alex
VP Product, NovaCare Analytics
From: maya_srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@novacare.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Apr 2028 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Runtime adoption — next steps for streaming & output contract

Alex — thanks for the clear asks and for sharing the draft schema. High level: we can meet your timeline. I'll own the MAP and Marissa will coordinate the CS handoff; Rishi will outline the adapter pattern and test harness.

Proposed mini-MAP (high level milestones):
1) Week 0–1: Finalize schema contract (Redwood + NovaCare) — expected deliverable: agreed JSON schema, canonical examples, and a small contract-test runner.
2) Week 2: Adapter prototype — a lightweight server (Node/Go) that demonstrates tool-call forwarding and auth handling; includes network diagram and endpoint_map_v2.png.
3) Week 3: Integration sprint — run streaming smoke tests against your staging, run contract tests, fix regressions.
4) Week 4: Cutover plan & SLA readout — ops runbook and rollback steps.

Rishi, can you confirm the recommended adapter pattern and what we should include in the contract-test runner? I'll draft the MAP workbook (mutual_action_plan_novacare.xlsx) and share a working copy.

Maya Srinivasan
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: maya_srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@novacare.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Apr 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Runtime adoption — recommended adapter & contract tests

Maya / team — technically: we recommend a thin 'adapter shim' that lives in NovaCare's network and performs three things:
- Authentication & token exchange (short-lived tokens from your authz to Redwood),
- Tool-call routing (map tool identifiers in the model output to internal service endpoints),
- Envelope -> canonical response transformation (wrap the model's streamed events into your claim objects).

Key implementation notes:
- Use our streaming SDK with the on-data callback; ensure you surface the model's function call events to the shim (we can provide an example in Node).
- For structured outputs, we suggest converting outputs to the "canonical_claim" schema we define, with a small shim library (open-source) for validation using AJV.
- Contract-test runner: a simple Docker image that runs a mocked Redwood runtime and your shim, then executes a set of input prompts and asserts the final JSON matches the schema (we'll provide a baseline set of tests).

I'll attach a short checklist in the shared Drive and a sample Node adapter snippet in the playbook link. If you want, I can drop a 30-min tech deep-dive next week.

—Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@novacare.ai>
To: maya_srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@novacare.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Apr 2028 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Runtime adoption — agreed MAP and procurement info

Thanks Maya & Rishi — that approach aligns with our security needs. We've run the draft schema by our engineering leads and have two small asks:
1) We need an explicit field-level stability table (which fields are beta vs guaranteed) in the schema doc.
2) Can Redwood include a lightweight webhook consumer example for tool-call callbacks (we use existing internal webhooks, want to see examples).

Procurement asked me to attach the initial P.O. guidance so legal can review terms during the MAP. I'm attaching a short P.O. note (sent internally). Once we have the MAP workbook and the stability table, procurement can move forward with a standard SOW template.

Alex
From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@novacare.ai>, maya_srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@novacare.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Runtime adoption — MAP workbook & next steps

Alex / team — appreciate the quick alignment. Maya and I have uploaded the working MAP workbook to the shared Drive (link below). Action items for this week:
- Redwood: finalize field-level stability table and add webhook consumer example to the adapter appendix (owner: Rishi).
- NovaCare: confirm staging endpoints and list of tool IDs to be proxied (owner: Alex).
- Procurement: review PO guidance and flag any contract changes (owner: Procurement Team).

I'll put a 30-min slot on calendars for Thursday to review the MAP together — invitation pending. If legal wants an early look at sample SOW language, I can share the template we use for Dedicated deals.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
